78: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE

A scenario file is a claim until someone runs its commands on a tree that contains phases 002 to 007. Without that run, phase 009 would measure templates while the playbook that describes them is untested.

83: ### Purpose
84: Every scenario this packet adds has a real execution record and a verdict that another person can check from the captured output.

90: ## 3. SCOPE
91: 
92: ### In Scope
93: - One disposable worktree created through `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh` from the operator's `BASE_REF`.
94: - Provisioning that worktree with its own dependency trees and its own build, proved by a realpath check.
95: - Literal execution of the eight scenarios phase 007 added, with output captured under `scratch/runs/`.
96: - A scripted compare of each run against a frozen pass pattern, with the scenario file's own Pass section as the fallback authority.
97: - At most three fix briefs and reruns for a failing scenario, then an escalation record.
98: - One report package with the real file set of an existing report folder, plus one row in the reports index.
99: - One read-only frontier review of the report and the runs.
100: 
101: ### Out of Scope
102: - Editing the scenario files. Phase 007 owns their text, and a scenario defect is escalated to its owner.
103: - Fixing product code by hand. A fix is one DeepSeek brief with one named file inside the disposable worktree.
104: - Measuring the authoring benchmark delta. Phase 009 owns that comparison.
105: - Committing or pushing. Both stay with the operator.
106: - Running anything in the primary checkout. The only scenario host is the disposable worktree.
107: 
108: ### Files to Change
109: 
110: | File Path | Change Type | Description |
111: |-----------|-------------|-------------|
112: | `scratch/scenarios.tsv`, `scratch/results.tsv`, `scratch/verdicts.md` | Create | Scenario map, verdict rows and the human-readable verdict page |
113: | `scratch/worktree/*`, `scratch/tools/*` | Create | Worktree proofs and the three scratch scripts |
114: | `scratch/runs/*`, `scratch/fix/*`, `scratch/fixes/*`, `scratch/review/*` | Create | Captured runs, fix briefs, the pre-removal patch and the review reply |

116: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/results.csv` | Create | One row per scenario |
117: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/source.md` | Create | Where the runs and the raw evidence live |
118: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/outcomes/<playbook-id>.json` | Create | One outcome record per scenario |
119: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/README.md` | Modify | One new row at the top of the run index |
120: | `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `goal.md`, `implementation-summary.md` | Modify | Progress and evidence |
121: <!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->

125: <!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->
126: ## 4. REQUIREMENTS
127: 
128: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)
129: 
130: | ID | Requirement |
131: |----|-------------|
132: | REQ-001 | The disposable worktree is created through `worktree-naming.sh create` from `BASE_REF`, its provisioning exits 0 and the own-code check prints no `FOREIGN` line. |
133: | REQ-002 | `scratch/scenarios.tsv` holds exactly eight rows, each row names an existing scenario file and no row is a duplicate. |
134: | REQ-003 | Every scenario row has a non-empty `scratch/runs/<playbook-id>.txt` and a verdict of `PASS`, `FAIL`, `FIXED`, `ESCALATED` or `SCENARIO_DEFECT` in `scratch/results.tsv`. |
135: | REQ-004 | The report package holds `README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md` and one `outcomes/<playbook-id>.json` per scenario, and `results.csv` holds eight data rows. |
136: | REQ-005 | The primary checkout status shows no change outside this phase folder, the new report folder and the one index row. When the conductor works in a build worktree, the primary checkout shows no change at all. |
137: | REQ-006 | The disposable worktree and its branch are removed after the evidence is copied, and the removal was allowed only when every changed path in `scratch/fixes/status.txt` appeared in `scratch/fixes/fix.patch`. |
138: 
139: ### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)
140: 
141: | ID | Requirement |
142: |----|-------------|
143: | REQ-007 | One read-only frontier review of the report and the runs ran, and each finding is applied or recorded in `goal.md` section 4 with the reason it was not. |
144: | REQ-008 | Every failed scenario has at most three fix briefs, each naming one file, and an `ESCALATED` row when the third fix did not pass. |
145: | REQ-009 | Before the worktree is removed, its diff and status are saved to `scratch/fixes/fix.patch` and `scratch/fixes/status.txt`, so a fix made inside the worktree survives as a patch. |
146: 
147: > Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,
148: > which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.
149: <!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->

154: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
155: 
156: - **SC-001**: Phase 009 can read `results.csv` and know which scenarios passed without opening a run file.
157: - **SC-002**: The operator can rerun the scenario set from the report's REPRODUCIBILITY section and get the same verdicts on the same `BASE_REF`.
158: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: <!-- ANCHOR:risks -->
163: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
164: 
165: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
166: |------|------|--------|------------|
167: | Dependency | `BASE_REF` contains the phase 002 to 007 changes | Every scenario tests an old tree and fails for the wrong reason | `tasks.md` T007 checks the card, both guard scripts and the v2.3 stamp inside the disposable worktree before the first run |
168: | Dependency | The disposable worktree gets its own `node_modules` and `dist` | The run silently uses the primary checkout code | `tasks.md` T006 rejects any realpath outside the worktree and stops on `FOREIGN` |
169: | Dependency | npm can install from the registry or the local cache | Provisioning fails and no scenario can run | `worktree-naming.sh create` reports the failing package, and `tasks.md` T006 retries provisioning once, then records the blocker |
170: | Risk | A scenario file is not copy-runnable | The run fails and looks like a product defect | The failure protocol names the scenario as the owner, records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and escalates to phase 007 |
171: | Risk | Worktree removal deletes the only copy of a run | The report loses its evidence | Every run is captured under `$PHASE/scratch/runs/` in the conductor's checkout before removal, and T016 checks eight recorded rows and every run file before it removes the worktree |
172: | Risk | A scenario leaves a throwaway track in the worktree | Removal is refused by the clean-status gate | The gate refuses removal while any changed path is missing from `scratch/fixes/fix.patch`, and T016 prints every changed path before it decides |
173: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: 
178: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
179: 
180: ### Performance
181: - **NFR-P01**: One scenario run is stopped by the runner's 30 minute alarm. A run that ends with `exit=142` is recorded as `TIMEOUT` and handled as a failure.
182: - **NFR-P02**: Provisioning the disposable worktree finishes within 45 minutes. A longer run is stopped and recorded as a blocker.
183: 
184: ### Security
185: - **NFR-S01**: No brief carries a credential, a token or a key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
186: - **NFR-S02**: Every worker runs with `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` and `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0`, and its brief states the child-dispatch exemption.
187: 
188: ### Reliability
189: - **NFR-R01**: A verdict comes from a captured output file and a frozen pattern, never from a chat message. A second conductor with the same files reaches the same verdict.
190: - **NFR-R02**: The report package is written after the last run and before the worktree is removed, so no evidence depends on a deleted directory.
191: 
192: ---
193: 
194: ## 8. EDGE CASES
195: 
196: ### Data Boundaries
197: - Empty input: a scenario file with no `### Commands` block is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is escalated, never executed from a guessed command.
198: - Maximum length: a run file above 2 MB is truncated by `run-scenario.sh` to its first 2 MB and last 200 lines, which writes a `truncated=yes` line that the comparator records in the verdict reason.
199: - Duplicate match: two playbook index rows that carry one S label's playbook id stop the map build with `AMBIGUOUS <S label>`, and no scenario runs until phase 007 is fixed.
200: 
201: ### Error Scenarios
202: - External service failure: a provider error stops the S8 dispatch. T010 records the error line, waits 10 minutes and retries once, then marks S8 `ESCALATED`.
203: - Network timeout: a provisioning failure is retried once with `worktree-naming.sh provision`. A second failure stops the phase with `BLOCKED provisioning`.
204: - Worktree removal refused: the gate names every changed path that is missing from `scratch/fixes/fix.patch`. When a path is listed, the worktree is kept and the operator is asked to decide.
205: 
206: ---
207: 
208: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
209: 
210: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
211: |-----------|-------|----------|
212: | Scope | 10/25 | Files: 8 scenarios read, 0 source files changed by hand. Systems: playbook, validator, guards, report index |
213: | Risk | 8/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: Y (the report index row) |
214: | Research | 8/20 | The scenario map is read from phase 007 and the report shape from an existing folder |
215: | Multi-Agent | 8/15 | Workstreams: one runner, one S8 worker, up to three fix workers, one reviewer |
216: | Coordination | 10/15 | Dependencies: `BASE_REF`, provider login, provisioning |
217: | **Total** | **44/100** | **Level 3** |
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
222: 
223: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
224: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
225: | R-001 | A scenario passes because the worktree ran the primary checkout's code | M | M | Own-code realpath check in T006 and a `FOREIGN` stop |
226: | R-002 | A scenario fails on a real product defect and the fix worker edits the wrong file | M | M | The fix brief names the `- Implementation:` file from the scenario's `## 4. SOURCE FILES` list and no other path |
227: | R-003 | The report is assembled from chat output rather than run files | M | L | Every report field is generated from `scratch/results.tsv` and the captured run files, and T017 reads the files |
228: | R-004 | The report index row is added twice on a rerun | L | M | T014 greps for the exact report folder name before it inserts the row |
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## 11. USER STORIES
233: 
234: ### US-001: One run per scenario (Priority: P0)
235: 
236: **As a** conductor, **I want** each scenario's own command block executed on a tree that holds every prior phase, **so that** the verdict describes the shipped behavior and not a retyped copy.
237: 
238: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
239: 
240: ---
241: 
242: ### US-002: Evidence after the worktree is gone (Priority: P0)
243: 
244: **As the** operator, **I want** every captured run and verdict to survive the disposable worktree, **so that** I can audit the phase without recreating it.
245: 
246: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
251: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
252: 
253: - None that block this phase. The one open input is the operator's `BASE_REF`, and `tasks.md` T001 stops the phase when it is absent.
254: - A scenario whose own Pass section disagrees with the frozen pass pattern is a phase 007 defect. The run records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and the phase continues with the other scenarios.
255: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->
256:

260: 
261: - **Implementation Plan**: See `plan.md`
262: - **Task Breakdown**: See `tasks.md`
263: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
264: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD

142: |----|-------------|
143: | REQ-007 | One read-only frontier review of the report and the runs ran, and each finding is applied or recorded in `goal.md` section 4 with the reason it was not. |
144: | REQ-008 | Every failed scenario has at most three fix briefs, each naming one file, and an `ESCALATED` row when the third fix did not pass. |
145: | REQ-009 | Before the worktree is removed, its diff and status are saved to `scratch/fixes/fix.patch` and `scratch/fixes/status.txt`, so a fix made inside the worktree survives as a patch. |
146: 
147: > Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,
148: > which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.
149: <!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: <!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
154: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
155: 
156: - **SC-001**: Phase 009 can read `results.csv` and know which scenarios passed without opening a run file.
157: - **SC-002**: The operator can rerun the scenario set from the report's REPRODUCIBILITY section and get the same verdicts on the same `BASE_REF`.
158: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: <!-- ANCHOR:risks -->
163: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
164: 
165: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
166: |------|------|--------|------------|
167: | Dependency | `BASE_REF` contains the phase 002 to 007 changes | Every scenario tests an old tree and fails for the wrong reason | `tasks.md` T007 checks the card, both guard scripts and the v2.3 stamp inside the disposable worktree before the first run |
168: | Dependency | The disposable worktree gets its own `node_modules` and `dist` | The run silently uses the primary checkout code | `tasks.md` T006 rejects any realpath outside the worktree and stops on `FOREIGN` |
169: | Dependency | npm can install from the registry or the local cache | Provisioning fails and no scenario can run | `worktree-naming.sh create` reports the failing package, and `tasks.md` T006 retries provisioning once, then records the blocker |
170: | Risk | A scenario file is not copy-runnable | The run fails and looks like a product defect | The failure protocol names the scenario as the owner, records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and escalates to phase 007 |
171: | Risk | Worktree removal deletes the only copy of a run | The report loses its evidence | Every run is captured under `$PHASE/scratch/runs/` in the conductor's checkout before removal, and T016 checks eight recorded rows and every run file before it removes the worktree |
172: | Risk | A scenario leaves a throwaway track in the worktree | Removal is refused by the clean-status gate | The gate refuses removal while any changed path is missing from `scratch/fixes/fix.patch`, and T016 prints every changed path before it decides |
173: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: 
178: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
179: 
180: ### Performance
181: - **NFR-P01**: One scenario run is stopped by the runner's 30 minute alarm. A run that ends with `exit=142` is recorded as `TIMEOUT` and handled as a failure.
182: - **NFR-P02**: Provisioning the disposable worktree finishes within 45 minutes. A longer run is stopped and recorded as a blocker.
183: 
184: ### Security
185: - **NFR-S01**: No brief carries a credential, a token or a key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
186: - **NFR-S02**: Every worker runs with `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` and `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0`, and its brief states the child-dispatch exemption.
187: 
188: ### Reliability
189: - **NFR-R01**: A verdict comes from a captured output file and a frozen pattern, never from a chat message. A second conductor with the same files reaches the same verdict.
190: - **NFR-R02**: The report package is written after the last run and before the worktree is removed, so no evidence depends on a deleted directory.
191: 
192: ---
193: 
194: ## 8. EDGE CASES
195: 
196: ### Data Boundaries
197: - Empty input: a scenario file with no `### Commands` block is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is escalated, never executed from a guessed command.
198: - Maximum length: a run file above 2 MB is truncated by `run-scenario.sh` to its first 2 MB and last 200 lines, which writes a `truncated=yes` line that the comparator records in the verdict reason.
199: - Duplicate match: two playbook index rows that carry one S label's playbook id stop the map build with `AMBIGUOUS <S label>`, and no scenario runs until phase 007 is fixed.
200: 
201: ### Error Scenarios
202: - External service failure: a provider error stops the S8 dispatch. T010 records the error line, waits 10 minutes and retries once, then marks S8 `ESCALATED`.
203: - Network timeout: a provisioning failure is retried once with `worktree-naming.sh provision`. A second failure stops the phase with `BLOCKED provisioning`.
204: - Worktree removal refused: the gate names every changed path that is missing from `scratch/fixes/fix.patch`. When a path is listed, the worktree is kept and the operator is asked to decide.
205: 
206: ---
207: 
208: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
209: 
210: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
211: |-----------|-------|----------|
212: | Scope | 10/25 | Files: 8 scenarios read, 0 source files changed by hand. Systems: playbook, validator, guards, report index |
213: | Risk | 8/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: Y (the report index row) |
214: | Research | 8/20 | The scenario map is read from phase 007 and the report shape from an existing folder |
215: | Multi-Agent | 8/15 | Workstreams: one runner, one S8 worker, up to three fix workers, one reviewer |
216: | Coordination | 10/15 | Dependencies: `BASE_REF`, provider login, provisioning |
217: | **Total** | **44/100** | **Level 3** |
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
222: 
223: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
224: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
225: | R-001 | A scenario passes because the worktree ran the primary checkout's code | M | M | Own-code realpath check in T006 and a `FOREIGN` stop |
226: | R-002 | A scenario fails on a real product defect and the fix worker edits the wrong file | M | M | The fix brief names the `- Implementation:` file from the scenario's `## 4. SOURCE FILES` list and no other path |
227: | R-003 | The report is assembled from chat output rather than run files | M | L | Every report field is generated from `scratch/results.tsv` and the captured run files, and T017 reads the files |
228: | R-004 | The report index row is added twice on a rerun | L | M | T014 greps for the exact report folder name before it inserts the row |
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## 11. USER STORIES
233: 
234: ### US-001: One run per scenario (Priority: P0)
235: 
236: **As a** conductor, **I want** each scenario's own command block executed on a tree that holds every prior phase, **so that** the verdict describes the shipped behavior and not a retyped copy.
237: 
238: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
239: 
240: ---
241: 
242: ### US-002: Evidence after the worktree is gone (Priority: P0)
243: 
244: **As the** operator, **I want** every captured run and verdict to survive the disposable worktree, **so that** I can audit the phase without recreating it.
245: 
246: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
251: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
252: 
253: - None that block this phase. The one open input is the operator's `BASE_REF`, and `tasks.md` T001 stops the phase when it is absent.
254: - A scenario whose own Pass section disagrees with the frozen pass pattern is a phase 007 defect. The run records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and the phase continues with the other scenarios.
255: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->
